resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register gives 3,129 ft (954 m), which matches the record. The project's home page and project history give 3,198 feet. The story gives both.

The register's 1961 build year is for the current CL-100 cab. Both the register and the project history say the first lookout on the site went into service in 1926 and was replaced in 1961, so the record's 1961 is correct for the current structure.

notes_for_editor: Access: the project site says the lookout, visitor center and gate are closed to visitation and the surrounding area is open when conditions allow. The pages are undated, so the story says 'at the moment' and access is set to closed as of 2026-10-08. Staffing ('volunteer', as_of is the read date) rests on the site's undated claim of an active volunteer base and seasonal internships; the site's 'now in our 30th year' line was not turned into a date. The record's kind 'two_story' is not contradicted by the register text (a CL-100 cab on a 10-foot block base) but is not clearly supported either; left unchanged. The 1959 newspaper item says the lookout house was blown down; it does not say the cab was rebuilt that year, and the story does not link it to the 1961 replacement. The 1930 newsletter is a California District News Letter item dated January 3, 1930; its Christmas Day date is the item's own. Staff names in the newspaper items are left out. The project history dates the Audubon falcon monitoring to the late 1970s and dates the neglect (some 15 years) to the late 1970s and 1980s; the story uses that period, and neither is recorded as a separate event. Search results included condor-site blog posts and a visitor listing that were not read and not used. Budget used: 5 distinct pages and 1 web search.
